title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. A binary tree's depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.
constraints: The depth of an empty tree is 0

examples.explanation: The longest path is 3 to 20 to 15, which contains three nodes.

hints.content: Ask the recursive question first: if I already knew the depth of both subtrees, what is the depth of the whole tree?
The path must go through one of the two children, so the answer is one plus the deeper child.
The deepest path can only be the left path or the right path, so take the maximum of the two.
Level order traversal with a queue also works: the number of levels is the depth, and the queue size is the width of each level.

invariant: Every call returns the correct maximum depth of its own subtree, so the parent only has to take the maximum and add itself.
whyThisPattern: The tree pattern is about defining the recursive call and combining the results. Depth is the simplest example of that: solve both children, take the larger answer, add one for the current node.
bruteForce: Walking every root to leaf path separately is exponential on a balanced tree because the shared upper part is visited again and again. One traversal of the tree is linear.
interviewExplanation: I solve the problem recursively: an empty subtree has depth zero, and for a node the maximum depth is one plus the larger depth of its two subtrees. Because each node is visited exactly once, this is linear in the number of nodes, with a recursion stack equal to the tree height.
commonMistakes: Returning 1 for an empty subtree instead of 0, which shifts every result by one.
Adding one to both children and taking the minimum instead of the maximum.
Forgetting that the depth counts nodes, so the leaf itself counts as 1.

animationSteps.title: The tree
animationSteps.description: Root 3 with children 9 and 20, and 15 and 7 under 20.
animationSteps.text: The tree has root 3, its left child 9, its right child 20, and 15 and 7 as the children of 20.

animationSteps.title: Empty subtrees
animationSteps.text: Node 9 has no children, so its left and right subtrees are empty and each has depth 0.

animationSteps.title: Predict the move
animationSteps.description: Both subtrees of the root return a depth. Which one wins?
animationSteps.text: For the root, the left subtree has depth 1 and the right subtree has depth 2. Choose the combination rule.

payload.prompt: left depth = 1, right depth = 2. What is the depth of the root?
payload.explanation: The deepest path goes through the deeper subtree, so the answer is one plus the maximum.

animationSteps.title: Combine at the root
animationSteps.text: The depth of the root is one plus the larger child depth, which is one plus two, so three.

animationSteps.title: Depth is 3
animationSteps.description: The longest path is 3 to 20 to 15.
animationSteps.text: The maximum depth is 3, found along the path 3, 20, 15.
